title: Pentachlorophenol effect on competitive sorption of some BTEXs on Algerian modified clays
content:
Abstract

This present study is devoted to the elimination by sorption of toluene (T), xylene (X), and pentachlorophenol (PCP) first in simple mono-component systems then in binary mixtures. Homoionic sodium montmorillonite (Na-Mt) as well as natural bentonite (Bt) that were used as precursors were separately intercalated by large hydroxyferric polycations and then co-inserted with hexadecyltrimethylammonium bromide (HDTMA) molecules to prepare new HDTMA-Fe-Bt and HDTMA-Fe-Mt sorbents. In single mono-component systems, kinetic results showed very fast pseudo-equilibrium states during the first contact hour. The subsequent sorption modeling indicated a complex kinetic mechanism, while the sorption isotherms were described by the Freundlich and Sips models. The effect of pH on the retention of each sorbate showed that the sorption of (PCP) strongly depends on the value of its pKa and the pHpzc of the sorbent, while the sorptions of (T) and (X) do not seem to be too much affected by the variation in pH due to their higher pKa. In binary mixtures, the corresponding results for all studied molar ratios (T/PCP) and (X/PCP) showed that the presence of (PCP) as a co-sorbate leads to an increase in sorption of (T) or (X) as the main solute. Sheindorf-Rebhun-Sheintuch (SRS) model allowed the determination of interaction coefficients (Sorbate/Co-Sorbate) with high correlation coefficient values for most ratios.
